title: HE HAD EVERY RIGHT TO DESTROY THEM… SO WHY DIDN’T HE?
paragraphs:
HE HAD EVERY RIGHT TO DESTROY THEM… SO WHY DIDN’T HE?
The shocking reason Joseph chose mercy over revenge—and what it exposes about your own heart
He stood in front of the very men who sold him like an animal.

They didn’t recognize him.
But he recognized everything.

The faces.
The voices.
The memories he tried to bury in prison walls and palace silence.

This was the moment every broken person secretly dreams about.
The moment where power flips.
Where the one who was humiliated finally gets to decide what happens next.
Joseph could have ended them.

No one would question him.
No one would stop him.
Egypt’s authority rested in his hands like a loaded weapon.
And yet… he wept.

Not out loud at first.
He turned away. Hid it.
Because something deeper than revenge was happening inside him.
And if you’re honest… this is where it starts to feel uncomfortable.

Because most of us don’t struggle to understand Joseph’s pain.
We struggle to understand his mercy.
Genesis 45:5 records his words, but when you lean into the Hebrew, it cuts deeper than surface reading:
“וְעַתָּה אַל־תֵּעָצְבוּ וְאַל־יִחַר בְּעֵינֵיכֶם כִּי־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי הֵנָּה כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹהִים לִפְנֵיכֶם”
“Now do not be grieved or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.”
Read that again slowly.

He didn’t deny what they did.
“מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי” — you sold me.

He didn’t excuse it.
He didn’t pretend it didn’t hurt.
But he saw something bigger than the betrayal.
He saw God in it.

Not approving evil…
But redeeming it.
This is where most people stop following the story, because this kind of perspective costs too much.
Joseph reframed his trauma through God’s sovereignty.

And that’s not easy theology…
That’s lived surrender.
Because let’s be honest.
You’ve replayed your own version of that moment.

The betrayal.
The rejection.
The lies spoken about you.
The people who smiled in front of you and cut you behind your back.

And somewhere deep inside…
you’ve imagined what it would feel like to make them feel it too.
To finally balance the scale.
To finally win.
Joseph had that chance.
And he refused it.
Why?
Because revenge would have made him like them.
But grace made him like God.
Romans 12:19 echoes this truth centuries later in Greek:
“Μὴ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκδικοῦντες… ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, λέγει κύριος.”
“Do not avenge yourselves… ‘Vengeance is mine, I will repay,’ says the Lord.”
Joseph trusted that.

Not emotionally.
Not instantly.
But deeply.

He allowed God to be the judge…
so he could become the vessel.
And this is where it confronts you.

Because holding onto revenge feels powerful…
but it’s actually a quiet prison.
Joseph had already been in chains.
He wasn’t about to go back—this time emotionally.
So he let it go.

Not because they deserved it…
but because God deserved his obedience.
And suddenly… the story shifts.
The boy who was thrown into a pit becomes the man who pulls others out of theirs.
The one who was stripped of his robe now covers others with provision.
The one who was forgotten becomes the reason others survive.
This is what grace does.

It doesn’t just heal you.
It transforms you into someone who heals others.
And if you’re reading this… something inside you is stirring.
Because you know exactly where this applies.
There’s a name in your mind right now.
A memory you still revisit.
A wound that hasn’t fully closed.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
So what are you going to do with it?
Joseph made a decision that most people never make.

He chose to trust God’s justice…
and walk in God’s mercy.
And that decision didn’t just change his story.
It preserved nations.
That’s how powerful obedience is.

So if something in you is tired of carrying bitterness…
if you’re exhausted from replaying pain…
if you’re ready to be free…
Don’t stay silent.
Your voice matters here.
And if you truly want to glorify God—not just in words, but in action—then stand with this mission.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is transformation.
This is discipleship.
This is war for souls.
And you’re not here by accident.
You were meant to read this.
You were meant to feel this.
You were meant to respond.

Because the same God who rewrote Joseph’s story…
is standing ready to rewrite yours.
And the question is—
Will you let Him?
